extra.text: An old man in a robe that was royal blue a long time ago is pinching dead leaves off his herbs. "You'll be the one from the sea. Orlen Vey. I was mage to the court in Zaron, once, when that meant something."
"Water first. It's everywhere: in the air, in the ground, in you. Ask it to come."
"Good. Now the other side of it."
Orlen doesn't look up from his herbs. "I've nothing to say to you."
"Come by whenever you like. Magic's mostly practice, and I've no one else to bore."

choices.label: "Will you teach me magic?"
choices.result: He looks at you properly for the first time. "Everyone has a little. Most never find it. Let's see if you're most." He sets an empty cup on the garden wall. "Water first. Ask it to come."

choices.label: Try to fill the cup
choices.result: Nothing. Nothing. Then a cold bead forms on the rim, and another, and the cup fills from the bottom up. "There," says Orlen. "Draw Water. It'll fill your waterskin, and it'll put out a small fire, which matters more than you'd think."

choices.label: "What comes next?"
choices.result: "Fire. The same pull, the other way." It takes you longer this time, and when the spark comes it nearly takes your eyebrows. Orlen chuckles. "Kindle. A spark, no more. Light my brazier there and we'll call it a day."

choices.label: "What happened in Zaron?"
choices.result: "King Melvin was a good man once. Fair. Stubborn. Then, a few years ago, something changed in him. His eyes went flat. He stopped sleeping. The taxes started." Orlen's hands go still on his herbs. "I told him something was wrong, and he thanked me for my service and sent me here. It isn't only him. Animals with yellow eyes. Wells that taste of iron. Something is getting into things."

scenes.title: Orlen's brazier
text: An iron brazier full of dry kindling.

extra.text: It's burning steadily. Orlen keeps feeding it sprigs of something that smells of pine.

scenes.title: Smoke
text: The kindling catches with a soft whump. Orlen opens his mouth to say something, and a bell starts clanging down in the village.
You both turn. Black smoke is rising from the harbour. "The net shed," says Orlen. "Dry nets go up like straw." He's already reaching for his stick. "Well. Lesson two."

choices.label: Run down to the village
choices.result: You run. Orlen follows as fast as his old legs let him.

choices.label: Stay here. It's not your shed
choices.result: Orlen looks at you for a long moment, then goes down the hill alone. By the time the bell stops, the net shed is ash, and half the nets in Skelmed with it.

extra.text: A wiry boy with Ida's red hair. "Snares are mine. Hands off, unless Ma says."
"Ma sent you? Rook. Snares are along this track, three of them. The last one's right up at the top. Something's been robbing it. I don't go up there now."
"Ma says you're all right. That's high praise, from her."
"Still can't believe we did it. Don't tell Ma I said that."

choices.label: "Got a spare hare?"
choices.result: Rook sighs and takes you down a line of his own you didn't know about. There's one hare in it. "Don't tell Ma."

scenes.title: A snare
text: A hare hangs limp in the wire loop of one of Rook's snares.

extra.text: Rook's snare. Not yours to take.

choices.label: Take the hare and reset the snare
choices.result: You work the hare free and set the loop again the way Rook had it.

scenes.title: A snare
text: Another of Rook's snares, and another hare in it.

extra.text: Rook's snare. Not yours to take.

choices.label: Take the hare and reset the snare
choices.result: Two. You're getting the knack of the wire.

scenes.title: The last snare
text: A wolf has its muzzle in the last snare, tearing at what's left of a hare. It lifts its head and looks at you. Yellow eyes.

extra.text: It goes back to eating. It's not your snare, and not your fight.

scenes.title: The snare robber
text: The wolf lies still. The hare it was eating is ruined, but in the brush beside the snare there's a second one, fresh, that it hadn't got to yet.

choices.label: Take it
choices.result: That's the snare line done.

scenes.title: The den
text: Bones, old and new, scattered round a hollow under the rocks. Something huge gets up out of it, unhurried, and shakes itself. Grey going black along the spine, a scar across its muzzle, and eyes like two coals.

extra.text: Rook nocks an arrow beside you. His hands are shaking, but the arrow isn't. "That's him," he breathes.
You're on your own. That's a bad idea.

choices.label: Back off, for now
choices.result: You back away slowly. The pack leader watches you go, and doesn't bother to follow.

scenes.title: Away
text: You break away and run, and the pack leader lets you. It doesn't need to chase. It knows where you'll be.

scenes.title: The pack leader
text: The great wolf goes down at last, and doesn't get up. Up close, under the grey, its skin is mottled purple, like a bruise that never healed.

extra.text: Rook lowers his bow and sits down hard on a rock. "We did it," he says, as if he doesn't believe it. Then, more quietly: "Did you see its eyes?"

choices.label: Skin it and take the pelt to Ida
choices.result: It's heavy, bloody work, and it takes a while.

scenes.title: The hill stream
text: The hill stream runs quick and cold over the stones.

choices.label: Fill the pail
choices.result: You fill the pail. It's heavy, and the path down is steep.

choices.label: Drink and fill your waterskin
choices.result: It tastes of moss and stone. You drink, then fill the skin.

scenes.title: The rock face
text: Rusty seams run through the rock where the old quarrymen stopped cutting.

extra.text: You'd need a pick. Garran has one.
That's three good lumps. Enough for Garran.

choices.label: Swing the pick
choices.result: Chips fly, and your arms ring with every blow. At last a lump of ore comes away, heavy and red-brown.

scenes.title: A glint
text: Something in the spoil heap at the foot of the rock face catches the light: a green stone the size of a fingernail, clear as bottle glass.

choices.label: Take it, to show Garran
choices.result: You wrap it in a scrap of cloth.

choices.label: Pocket it. Nobody would ever know
choices.result: It goes in your pocket, and stays there.

scenes.title: Yarrow
text: Yarrow: flat white flower heads on feathery stems. Packed into a wound, it keeps it clean. It'll grow back.

choices.label: Pick some
choices.result: You pick a good handful and fold it into a cloth.

scenes.title: Yarrow
text: Yarrow: flat white flower heads on feathery stems. Packed into a wound, it keeps it clean. It'll grow back.

choices.label: Pick some
choices.result: You pick a good handful and fold it into a cloth.

scenes.title: A young willow
text: A young willow leaning over the stream. Its bark brings a fever down, chewed or brewed. Take a little and it'll mend.

choices.label: Strip some bark
choices.result: You peel a few strips from the side facing the water, and leave the rest.
